svg.title: init repairs its own GitLab connection when something breaks it — init repairs a tampered variable and purges duplicate tokens
svg.text: init repairs its own GitLab connection when something
Scenario: init repairs a tampered variable and purges duplicate tokens

g.text: Given a project the framework already set up and is healthy
A fresh project after its first `task devsecops:init`, working correctly: one automation
token on the access-tokens page. Off-camera: the lambda user, the fresh project, the setup
that ran init once.
When a duplicate automation token is planted behind the framework's
back
A second token with the same name is created from outside the framework: the access-tokens
page now lists two automation tokens where there should be one. The test also checks through
the API that two are active.
And the CI/CD variable is overwritten with a bad value
The CI/CD variable is tampered with (its value replaced by a bad string, hidden on screen by
GitLab's own masking): the CI/CD variables page still lists it. The test also checks through
the API that its value is now the bad one.
And the developer runs the framework's init once more
A single `task devsecops:init` re-run: the finishing message shows it removed the duplicate
token and put the CI/CD variable back. The test also checks the command succeeded.
Then only one automation token survives the purge
The access-tokens page is back to a single automation token — the duplicate is gone. The
test also checks through the API that exactly one is active.
And the healed CI/CD variable clones the repository again
The variable no longer carries the bad value: it signs in to GitLab again and lists the
repository (the secret and commit IDs are masked). The test also checks through the API that
the value is no longer the tampered one, and does a full clone with it.
